subject: Discovery recap: embeddings & reranking for BrightCart (index scale, latency targets)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference>

Subject: Discovery recap: embeddings & reranking for BrightCart (index scale, latency targets)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the open items I captured so we’re aligned heading into a POC discussion. Please correct anything I got wrong or missing.

Summary of pain points
- Current search/recommendation quality drops on long-tail SKUs; manual tuning of re-rankers is time-consuming.
- High variance in latency during peak traffic (holiday spikes).
- Current cost of running experiments and production embeddings is increasing as catalog grows.

Current stack (as described)
- Vector storage / ANN: FAISS-based service backed by S3 snapshots (self-hosted).
- Metadata & search: Elasticsearch for faceting and textual search.
- Caching: Redis for hot results and session caches.

Workload & index scale
- Current vector index: ~3.0M product vectors (you mentioned ~2.8–3.1M range).
- Expected growth: ~3–4x over 12 months (catalog and derived embeddings).
- Typical queries: product-to-product recommendations and query reranking of top-200 results.

Performance targets / success criteria
- End-to-end reranking (search + embedding similarity + model rerank where applicable): target P95 <= 150ms; ideal target <= 100ms for 95% of traffic.
- Pure embedding similarity lookups (approx nearest neighbors): target median latency < 30–50ms.
- Quality: measurable uplift in CTR / add-to-cart for rerank experiments; baseline + 7–12% target improvement for initial POC.
- Cost sensitivity: aim to keep incremental inference cost predictable and < $X per 1k requests (we’ll provide a ballpark once we see sample volumes).

Batching / ingestion patterns
- Nightly bulk ingest: ~250k–350k new/updated vectors (batch-friendly).
- Near-real-time updates: smaller bursts for inventory and personalization (~10–100 updates/sec peak; often small bursts rather than sustained QPS).

POC scope & next steps (proposed)
1) We’ll do a single-model POC focusing on reranking for the product recommendations flow (top-200 -> rerank top-10).
2) BrightCart provides a sample export (we requested ~100k vectors + metadata + representative query logs).
3) Redwood will run two evaluation runs: ANN-only baseline (existing approach) vs Redwood inference+re-rank pipeline and report latency/cost/quality deltas.
4) Target metrics to measure: P50/P95 latency, throughput at 50 qps, vector recall@k, business metric proxy (CTR).

Open asks for you (what we need to start)
- Share the sample export (product vectors + metadata + 1 week of query logs) — you mentioned you can provide this as NDJSON.
- Confirm the data sharing path (S3 bucket link or secure Drive share) and whether we should route through your security contact for access.
- Any compliance constraints (SOC2 controls, IP restrictions) beyond standard NDA?

Attachments: brightcart-discovery-notes.pdf (summary of call, screenshots you shared).

Suggested timeline
- Sample data shared by end of week -> 1-week ingestion & baseline run -> 1-week evaluation and write-up.

If that all looks good, I’ll follow up with a short convo to lock dates and assign Dev for sandbox access.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

This is great, thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side so you have the correct numbers for sizing the POC: 
- Current index size is 2.8M product vectors (good to plan for 3M baseline).
- Nightly bulk ingest is closer to 250k items (we said 300k on the call; 250k is the steady-state we see).
- Real-time updates are smaller: mostly single-item updates from our inventory service (peaks up to ~60 updates/sec during bursts, but sustained is much lower).
- Regarding vector DB: we currently use a FAISS pipeline that writes periodic snapshots to S3 and an internal service for ANN queries. We are evaluating Pinecone and Milvus for managed options.

I attached a small sample export (product_vectors_sample.ndjson) and a link to an internal doc that explains our vector schema.

Can you provide a 2–3 sentence ballpark on pricing structure for a POC (bandwidth for embedding compute + serving tier)? I know it’s early but even rough guidance helps our procurement planning. Also, let’s tentatively target kickoff next Tue (8/11) if that works for your team.

Thanks —
Alex

Thanks for the summary, Marissa — and Alex for the sample. Quick internal note / proposed POC approach: 

POC playbook (high level)
- Ingest the 100k sample into a sandbox Redwood private instance configured to mirror BrightCart's production settings (index sharding & cache sizes).
- Run baseline ANN (FAISS) + our rerank pipeline to compare quality and end-to-end latency at controlled QPS (10, 25, 50).
- Report: P50/P95 latencies, tokens & GPU seconds for embedding compute, cost estimate for 1M QPS-month usage, and CTR proxy measurement.

Acceptance criteria for moving to a pilot
- P95 end-to-end rerank < 120ms at 50 qps load on sandbox (within 20% of production traffic characteristics).
- Successful integration with BrightCart's identity & ingestion (S3 presigned or direct upload).
- Security checklist signed off by BrightCart security for the sandbox environment.

Dev — can you confirm typical sandbox specs we should provision (GPUs, memory)? Also please prepare a short checklist for the data ingest (expected NDJSON fields, any transforms).

Marissa — I’ll draft a short statement of work / POC scope we can use to get procurement moving once Alex confirms the kickoff date.
